tara: FYI experiencing a weird case where the final SSE chunk disappears during an auth refresh/backoff sequence in the Go sample app. Repro is intermittent but consistent under load. :thinking:

kevin: can you paste the minimal repro and any logs? is this only Go?

tara: minimal repro attached below. quick notes:
- Start long-running streaming completion (~60s)
- Force token refresh during stream (shorten expiry in sample)
- Client does auth-refresh/backoff -> reconnect flow
- Sometimes last 'data: [DONE]' or final JSON chunk never arrives to client, stream just ends silently. :confused:

morgan: we've seen parity differences: python sdk (aiohttp) tends to reassemble the final fragment reliably, go's http client seems to drop final partial fragment when connection is aborted concurrently.

tara: logs (server + client excerpts):
```
SERVER: chunk seq=124 sent payload_len=1024 flags=CONT
SERVER: chunk seq=125 sent payload_len=512 flags=CONT
SERVER: chunk seq=126 sent payload_len=128 flags=FINAL
CLIENT: recv 124 (1024)
CLIENT: recv 125 (512)
CLIENT: connection reset during recv of seq=126, bytes_read=64
```

kevin: that looks like the client-level read was aborted while the server finished sending final chunk. Are we seeing resume tokens that include partial seq info?

tara: resume token currently encodes last fully processed token index; when final chunk is partially received we have no way to advertise 'I need the rest of seq=126' so server assumes client got it. Hence data loss.

alex: possible fixes I can think of:
- server side: ensure final chunk is idempotent and re-sent on reconnect based on sequence number (requires chunk-level ACKs)
- runtime: buffer final chunk until read completed and only expose stream-close when client acked full chunk (complicates throughput)
- sdk workaround: on auth-refresh abort, don't immediately reconnect — try gentle drain/wait for small grace period to allow final chunk to arrive (e.g., 100-300ms)

kevin: for parity, we should also audit other SDKs behavior on race between auth refresh and streaming reads. can you capture a HAR or tcpdump of one failing repro?

tara: attaching small curl repro that sometimes fails locally (use short expiry token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood/test/stream?length=60s"
```

morgan: quick note: Python rounds up partial reads differently which explains parity difference — but we should not rely on client heuristics.

tara: current mitigation: bump token refresh threshold in go-sample to avoid mid-stream refresh; added note in sample app README. This reduces but does not eliminate failures.

kevin: action items:
- kevin -> create runtime ticket to add a small final-chunk durability check / deterministic re-sent-final-chunk behavior (ENG-RT-4721) :memo:
- alex -> prototype server-side seq-based re-send logic for FINAL chunks (POC this week) :hammer_and_wrench:
- morgan -> run cross-sdk parity test harness against repro and add to CI (target: detect final-chunk-loss) :robot_face:
- tara -> add clear doc comment and README workaround in go-sample, link repro to ticket

dev-bot: Created issue ENG-RT-4721 and linked this thread.

kevin: thanks — let's validate fix with a stress test (1000 streams) and verify last_message_ts/logs for dropped final seqs. If we can't add seq-ACKs quickly, runtime buffering + short grace period seems safest short-term.

tara: noted. I'll start stress job and share results here. :eyes:

morgan: +1 on adding parity tests. also flagging SDK maintainers so we don't diverge silently.

kevin: assigning to eng-runtime and SDK leads. Will follow up in ENG-RT-4721.

tara: thanks all — filed the lightweight repro in the devex repo: github.com/redwood/devex/sse-final-chunk-repro and updated sample README with the temporary workaround.
